baseline_report: The patient has 10-year progressive bilateral visual loss with severe field constriction and no afferent pupillary defect, most consistent with chronic bilateral primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). The absence of bitemporal hemianopia refutes a compressive chiasmal lesion. Fundus autofluorescence hyperfluorescent foci raise retinal dystrophy as an important differential and argue against primary optic neuropathy. However, intraocular pressure, cup-to-disc ratio, OCT retinal nerve fiber layer thickness, and visual field pattern were not obtained, and electroretinography/genetic testing are unavailable, so confidence is moderate. POAG remains the leading diagnosis, but confirmatory ophthalmic testing is required to exclude retinal dystrophy and finalize the diagnosis.
